gates.question: What does census.py dispatch do in a checkout whose path holds .claude/worktrees, where the CLI denies its Edit allow rules of the owned files?

notes: Premise: census.py has no handling of a checkout path under .claude/worktrees, so dispatch pays for sessions whose Edit is denied. Premise run 2026-10-12: grep of _tools/census.py for 'worktrees' finds nothing and the repro fails; reproduces. Absorbs ST-lihlbwty (the warning before the paid run and the kb-census skill sentence for the interim). Gate g1 answered refuse: no spend is made when the path makes the edits impossible; the Edit rule form the CLI honours there is not planned (it needs a paid probe). Planned at the 2026-10-12 draft triage (sprint 8 of 19, "Census and fact diff: anchor runs write only their own rows, judge confirms are sampled, cost figures are measured"): it fixes a failure that recurred in recent sprints and blocks the EP-gzr4mmkm fitness test that a content sprint lands on headless Sonnet workers with no operator step beyond its gates. The kb states the likely cause: an edit under a protected directory such as .claude is denied under dontAsk (public/claude/settings-and-scopes.md:65, DOC); whether the CLI protects .claude/worktrees by path or by the rule form is what the planned refusal does not need to know.
